daily.title: Alexander Zverev faces fresh lawsuit from ex-girlfriend
daily.summary: World No. 1 tennis player Alexander Zverev is facing a new lawsuit related to a domestic abuse trial. The lawyer for his ex-girlfriend, Brenda Patea, told DW what the allegations are against the German player.

daily.title: EU Commission confirms it was targeted in cyberattack using AI tools
daily.summary: The European Commission was targeted by an "AI-generated cybercampaign," a spokesperson has said. This is the first time the bloc has publicly reported an AI-based cyberattack.

daily.title: No mention of fossil fuels in latest COP31 draft deal
daily.summary: One of the most fraught debates at the UN climate talks in Turkey has revolved around the future of coal, oil and gas. Now all mention of fossil fuels has been removed from the summit's new draft agreement.

daily.title: Wadephul: 'Coalition of the Willing' talks in Berlin send strong signal to Moscow
daily.summary: German Foreign Minister Wadephul has said the Coalition of the Willing meeting in Berlin sends a clear message to Moscow to take peace talks seriously. He also warned Ukraine should be prepared for peace talks to fail.

daily.title: Pakistan minister to visit India, but no breakthrough expected
daily.summary: A Pakistani minister's visit to India for a Shanghai Cooperation Organization forum marks a rare high-level contact between the two archrivals, but analysts say it does not signal a resumption of bilateral engagement.

daily.title: APEC summit: Trump, Xi, Putin talks end with 'peace declaration'
daily.summary: The three world leaders discussed the Russian invasion of Ukraine as well as nuclear arms controls. Following the trilateral talks, President Trump reportedly headed to the airport. Follow DW live.

daily.title: Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya, top UN court rules
daily.summary: The International Court of Justice has upheld large parts of a genocide case against Myanmar linked to the 2017 conflict with its Rohingya minority. It called for it to pay reparations and let refugees return safely.

daily.title: Germany news: Pistorius to visit Auschwitz memorial in Poland trip
daily.summary: Germany's Defense Minister's first stop in Poland will be at the memorial site of the former Nazi extermination camp Auschwitz-Birkenau. Follow DW for more.

daily.title: Denmark ratifies security deal with US and Greenland
daily.summary: The deal provides the US with expanded military access, on top of what it already had based on a previous agreement. It comes after threats by US President Trump to take Greenland with force.

daily.title: South Korea's top court overturns jail term for former PM Han
daily.summary: Former Prime Minister Han Duck-so was convicted of helping legitimize the 2024 martial law declaration. The case will now return to a lower court.

daily.title: Iran balances ties with China and Russia as Trump ramps up pressure
daily.summary: As Donald Trump seeks to tighten economic pressure on Iran, China remains its biggest oil customer and Russia a key partner. But both powers are balancing support for Tehran against broader interests with Washington.

daily.title: India: Nearly 50,000 evacuated as Cyclone Akvan nears the coast
daily.summary: Cyclone Akvan, the third severe storm to hit India's east coast in a month, is expected to make landfall on November 20. Meanwhile, PM Modi led a meeting of his Council of Ministers.

daily.title: What makes 'Grand Theft Auto VI' more than just a game?
daily.summary: When "GTA VI" is released on November 19, millions of people worldwide will rush to their consoles to play it. How has this video game created such a cross-generational buzz?

daily.title: Is the AI bubble bursting just as Anthropic goes public? Or is AI, with hundreds of billions still being invested, as strong as ever?
daily.summary: The sharp sell-off in tech stocks after the US midterms and the Nvidia scandal has cast doubt on Anthropic's IPO. Yet with hundreds of billions still being invested, some think the AI party is still in full swing.

daily.title: Crimean Bridge has been attacked again, Russian official says
daily.summary: The Crimean Bridge has been attacked again, Crimea's Russian-installed governor said. The attack comes as Vladimir Putin prepares to sit down with Donald Trump and Xi Jinping for joint talks in China.

daily.title: Ukraine's allies attend 'Coalition of the Willing' summit in Berlin
daily.summary: Ukraine's European backers are convening in Berlin, with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner also set to attend the meeting. Follow the latest.

daily.title: Almost 1 in 4 children live in conflict zones — report
daily.summary: Denial of humanitarian access, abductions and sexual violence are among several violations against children that have increased dramtically over the past year, according to a new report by Save the Children.

daily.title: Grand Theft Auto VI launches to global fanfare
daily.summary: After 13 years of waiting, fans around the world will get to play the latest installment in the blockbuster video game series. In focus: A tale of crime and violence in a fictionalized version of Miami.

daily.title: What the Crimean bridge attack means for Russia
daily.summary: Ukraine's latest strike on the Kerch Bridge has disrupted a key transport link between Russia and Crimea. Beyond the damage, the attack could have serious consequences for Russian military logistics and Putin's prestige.

daily.title: US Pentagon chief Hegseth signs military deal in Venezuela
daily.summary: On a visit to Caracas, Pete Hegseth signed a deal that signifies the "reestablishment of our defense partnership." US-Venezuela ties were strained for years until US troops ousted ex-President Nicolas Maduro in January.

daily.title: Borussia Dortmund bows to fan pressure and end Rheinmetall deal
daily.summary: Borussia Dortmund has reluctantly ended its association with a major sponsor after long-term fan protests. They are not the first Bundesliga club to u-turn, as commercial interests clash with politics and fan culture.

weekly.title: 'Coalition of the Willing' meets in Berlin: Europe remains committed to Ukraine
weekly.summary: The "Coalition of the Willing" supporting Ukraine is gathering in Berlin. One of the key issues under discussion is whether Europe will be able to play a role in future negotiations over the country's future.

weekly.title: Has the 'Parthenon puzzle' been solved? The long quest to reassemble lost eastern pediment
weekly.summary: The depiction of the birth of the goddess Athena above the Parthenon's entrance is considered a masterpiece of ancient art. Now, a German research team has pieced together all the surviving fragments.

weekly.title: How a green economy could help reverse climate change
weekly.summary: Green growth promises a future in which economies thrive without destroying the environment. But is this vision realistic?

weekly.title: Hashim Thaci's second conviction in The Hague reignites debate in Kosovo about justice and the Kosovo Specialist Chambers
weekly.summary: Former President Hashim Thaci has been convicted of trying to influence witnesses in his war crimes trial. The conviction has reignited debate in Kosovo about the Kosovo Specialist Chambers, the court that convicted him.

weekly.title: Back to 1997: Russia wants NATO to roll back its eastern expansion
weekly.summary: The Kremlin is reportedly calling on NATO to withdraw from large parts of Eastern Europe. What this would mean for the security of millions of Europeans — and what lies behind Russia's plan.

weekly.title: Rights court rules Turkey must release jailed lawmaker Atalay
weekly.summary: The European Court of Human Rights has called for the release of imprisoned elected lawmaker Can Atalay. Atalay has been in prison for almost five years despite rulings from the Turkish Constitutional Court.

weekly.title: Nvidia forms national security committee after Huang affair
weekly.summary: Nvidia has created a board-level committee for national security and export control. This follows the resignation of CEO Jensen Huang over extramarital affairs, allegedly including one with a Chinese intelligence asset.

weekly.title: Students' List candidates take seats as Serbian parliament opens
weekly.summary: Serbia's Student List's candidates have taken their oaths in the inaugural parliament session. As the new majority, they have 90 days to form a government.

weekly.title: Klopp and Wirtz offer glimpse of bright German future
weekly.summary: Germany's fall from grace in recent years has seen the team drift away from the fans. But Monday's drubbing of the Netherlands and the impact of Jürgen Klopp, Florian Wirtz and emerging youngsters offers hope.

weekly.title: Could the Airbus €3 billion loan row reignite a US-EU trade dispute?
weekly.summary: The US says a record €3 billion financing package for Airbus may conflict with a transatlantic aircraft-subsidy truce. EU officials insist the funding complies with market-based rules.

weekly.title: Germany news: Plans for Rwanda migrant hub come under fire
weekly.summary: Human rights groups have slammed plans by Germany and four other EU states to send rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda. In other news, business start-ups in Germany are on track to reach the highest level since 2015.

weekly.title: France's Philippe Diallo to challenge Infantino for FIFA presidency
weekly.summary: Philippe Diallo is the second candidate to stand against incumbent Gianni Infantino. He is backed by European football's governing body UEFA, known to be critical of Infantino.

weekly.title: NASA's Voyager 1 reaches a light-day away from Earth
weekly.summary: When just saying 'hello' takes a two-day round trip, you're a light-day, or 26 billion kilometers, from Earth. Only one human-made object has ever traveled that far — and its journey into interstellar space continues.

weekly.title: What has changed in James Bond films over the decades
weekly.summary: In 1962, a martini-drinking womanizer saved the world for the first time in "Dr. No." As Robert Pattinson takes on the role of 007, here's how the films evolved.

weekly.title: The AfD and neo-Nazi networks: How close are the connections?
weekly.summary: The Alternative for Germany party (AfD) has become a focal point for the far right. Many of its members and staff have ties to ethnonationalist or neo-Nazi organizations.

weekly.title: COP31 draft deal calls for 'immediate' shift away from fossil fuels
weekly.summary: The preliminary agreement at UN climate talks in Turkey calls for a rapid reduction of planet-warming emissions and at least $120 billion to help countries adapt to climate change.

weekly.title: Klopp wants Infantino out as FIFA candidate deadline looms
weekly.summary: Germany coach Jürgen Klopp has joined the chorus of football figures critical of FIFA President Gianni Infantino. But with time running out, there are few who seem willing to run against him.

weekly.title: Germany news: Merz, Söder aim to revisit electricity tax cut
weekly.summary: The Christian Democrats are in Munich, pushing to revive some tax relief that didn't make it into the budget after talks last week. And Manuela Schwesig faces a vote on a new term as regional leader. Follow DW.

weekly.title: Can a 'coalition of the willing' create momentum for a fossil fuel phaseout?
weekly.summary: In April, about 60 countries held an unprecedented meeting in Colombia to work out a plan to slowly quit oil, coal and gas. How influential is this coalition at the COP31 climate summit?

weekly.title: AI in classrooms: Fighting the great 'dumbing down'
weekly.summary: Research suggests that students who aren't careful about how they use ChatGPT and other AI tools risk poorer academic outcomes. It's a huge challenge for teachers.

weekly.title: German economy returns to growth, so why is the country still worried?
weekly.summary: The German economy is growing again, albeit slightly. However, economists warn that without reforms, higher productivity and solid public finances, a loss of prosperity and growing debt threaten future generations.

weekly.title: Despite restrictive abortion laws, Poland's 'Abortomat' — a locker that dispenses abortion pills — helps women who want to end a pregnancy
weekly.summary: Abortion laws in Poland are very restrictive. Activists there have found a new way to help women wanting to terminate a pregnancy: the "Abortomat," a locker that dispenses abortion pills. But they face fierce opposition.

weekly.title: Germany news: Germany holds national day of remembrance
weekly.summary: Events were held for "Volkstrauertag," a day commemorating victims of war and oppression. Meanwhile, experts said the country is headed for a budget crisis.

weekly.title: How AI is likely to change Germany's job market
weekly.summary: The scale of the economic disruption caused by AI has led even conservative politicians to talk about universal basic income. But economists aren't convinced, and campaigners think we need to ask deeper questions.

weekly.title: Germany's 2027 budget: A record €561 billion and a mountain of debt
weekly.summary: The 2027 federal budget proposal has finally been hammered out and is set for a vote in parliament. What are the government's policy priorities in defense, infrastructure, the economy and social spending?

weekly.title: Werner Holzer Prize awarded to Katja Gloger and DW's Jaafar Abdul Karim
weekly.summary: DW journalist Jaafar Abdul Karim and Russia correspondent Katja Gloger have been awarded the prestigious Werner Holzer Prize for international journalism.

weekly.title: Ukraine: Zelenskyy says security deal could go to referendum
weekly.summary: The US has broached the idea of Kyiv giving up the Donbas region in exchange for NATO membership, the Ukrainian president said.

weekly.title: Wolf Biermann at 90: The singer who defied East Germany
weekly.summary: His life is a reflection of contemporary German history, addressed via his songs and sharp wit. At 90, he's as feisty as ever.

weekly.title: Turkey uses espionage accusations to pressure government critics
weekly.summary: The arrest of a German foundation's employee in Istanbul this week has put the focus back on pressure tactics used by the Erdogan administration. The arrest is far from the first of its kind.

weekly.title: Gen Z protests: Do Baby Boomers really have it better than young people?
weekly.summary: Should young people in Germany be more worried about their future than Baby Boomers were in the 1980s and 1990s? Or should both generations take to the streets and protest together? DW checked the data.

weekly.title: The dangers of revising Europe's security architecture
weekly.summary: Experts warn against revising Europe's security framework because they say it would mean granting Moscow its longstanding wish of renegotiating postwar security on the continent.

weekly.title: What's going on with the polar vortex?
weekly.summary: Observations show the ring of fierce winds that rotate at the Earth's North Pole has changed direction. Scientists say it's a historic disruption and the earliest reversal on record. What could it mean for the weather?

weekly.title: Ice hockey impasse as Russia threatens sanctions on Canada, Germany
weekly.summary: Two weeks after the CAS ordered ice hockey's governing body to reintegrate Russia into international play, a solution remains elusive. Now Russia has threatened to take legal action against two tournament hosts.

weekly.title: Germany gives sweeping powers to police, intelligence services
weekly.summary: Drone sightings and cyberattacks have heightened security concerns. How are the police preparing to meet these challenges? And how do intelligence services plan to counter threats from both domestic and foreign sources?

weekly.title: Germany's Nmecha won't repeat controversial goal celebration
weekly.summary: Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp has said midfielder Felix Nmecha will not repeat a goal celebration that sparked controversy over the past week. Germany are set to face Serbia and the Netherlands in the Nations League.

weekly.title: Germany news: Parliament agrees on debt-laden 2027 budget
weekly.summary: The budget committee in the Bundestag worked into the night to sign off on next year's spending plans. These include levels of new debt only eclipsed once, at the height of the COVID pandemic. DW has more.

weekly.title: Czechia braces for massive protest against public media reform plans
weekly.summary: A fast-tracked bill to cut public media funding has sparked strikes, rallies and fears for the independence of public broadcasting in Czechia. A massive protest is planned for Prague on Sunday.

weekly.title: Could lack of money sink TFFF rainforest fund before it even launches?
weekly.summary: The TFFF rainforest fund aims to make forest conservation more profitable than deforestation. But a lack of money may prevent it from getting off the ground.

weekly.title: Iranian activist and Nobel Peace Prize winner Narges Mohammadi shares her story in memoir
weekly.summary: Written and smuggled out of prison, the 2023 Nobel Prize laureate's memoir reveals the cost of defying Iran's regime and fighting for freedom.

weekly.title: EU leaders tussle over whom to send to Ukraine, Russia peace talks
weekly.summary: A seat at the table for Europe now appears likely following comments by a US envoy who just held talks with Putin. But who will take that seat remains unclear.

weekly.title: Can the EU make it harder to trick consumers online?
weekly.summary: The EU wants to curb subscription traps, misleading sales tactics and features that keep people scrolling. What would the proposed Digital Fairness Act change, and does it go far enough?

weekly.title: What have the talks with Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi achieved for Ukraine?
weekly.summary: The first trilateral talks between Ukraine, the US and Russia in nine months have ended with an agreement on exchanging prisoners. Does this mark a genuine breakthrough and a step toward peace?

weekly.title: Hungary eases abortion restrictions in women's rights overhaul
weekly.summary: The reforms mark a break the the conservative policies of former PM Viktor Orban. The controversial "heartbeat regulation" is to be scrapped and women are to be better protected against violence.
